description.narrative: The Project is expected to have the following Development Impact: (i) Stakeholders effect - Increased access to Climate Finance: This Project supports JAB's development of sustainable financing, particularly for SMEs. IFC's investment and potential advisory is expected to grow JAB's climate finance portfolio significantly, with a focus on green buildings, renewable energy, and energy efficiency, thereby contributing to a reduction in GHG emissions; (ii) Stakeholders effect - Increased access to finance for WSMEs: The project is designed to empower women-owned and women-led SMEs in Jordan by increasing their access to finance, aiming to grow the Banks WSME loan portfolio, thus this initiative is expected to address the low economic participation of women and the challenges faced in accessing financial services; and (iii) Contribution to Market Creation - Sustainability: IFC anticipates that the Project will promote sustainability through the issuance of the one of the first sustainability bonds in the country that will set standards for further such issuances and increase overall climate, SME, and gender financing in Jordan.

The proposed investment entails an (i) IFC subscription of up to US$50 million in a sustainability bond to be issued by Jordan Ahli Bank Plc (JAB or the Bank) in Jordan covering the full amount at issuance and (ii) the provision by IFC of trade finance line of up to US$40 million under the Global Trade Finance Program (GTFP) for up to one year tenor (the Project). The bond will be structured in alignment with the International Capital Market Authority (ICMA) Sustainability Bond Guidelines (SBG), as confirmed by a Second Party Opinion (SPO) provider, and will aim to finance JAB's sustainability assets, including loans towards climate projects and women-owned or women led Small and Medium Enterprises (WSMEs). The Project is expected to be supported by Global SME Facility (GSMEF) as described in the Blended Finance Section.
